questions.question: What is the primary benefit of Syntax Highlighting?
options: It automatically fixes your code for you
It uses different colors to help you spot errors and understand code structure
It makes the code run faster in the terminal
It translates Python into other languages
questions.explanation: Syntax Highlighting color-codes different parts of your code (like strings, comments, and keywords). This makes it easier to read and helps you notice if you've made a typo when the colors don't look right.

questions.question: What happens when you click the 'v' or '>' icon next to a line number?
options: It deletes the code on that line
It collapses (folds) or expands blocks of code
It changes the code's font size
questions.explanation: This is called Code Folding. It allows you to hide large sections of code that you aren't currently working on, keeping your editor window clean and focused.

questions.question: Where should you look to find the specific tasks you need to complete for an exercise?
options: The Exercise Instructions at the top of the editor
questions.explanation: The 'Exercise Instructions' (labeled as point 2 in our layout) tell you exactly what you need to code to pass the lesson and earn your XP.

questions.question: What does the 'Download' button in the editor allow you to do?
options: Save your code to run in a local IDE like VS Code or PyCharm
Download more themes for the website
Update the Python version in your browser
questions.explanation: The Download button (point 8) lets you take the starter code off the platform so you can practice using professional development tools on your own computer.
